title: Occupational Therapy - Other Letter - Sophie Martin
writingTask: Using the information in the case notes, write a letter to Mr David Price, Workplace Rehabilitation Coordinator, Studio North Ltd, 50 Market Street, Nottingham, outlining the workplace adjustments and phased return-to-work plan recommended for Ms Martin.
caseNotes: You are an occupational therapist in an outpatient hand and work-rehabilitation service. Ms Sophie Martin is preparing to return to work after treatment for repetitive strain symptoms.
MEDICAL HISTORY: Right wrist and forearm overuse pain - 4 months
Symptoms aggravated by prolonged mouse use and drawing tablet
Frequent use of mouse and digital pen
Off work for 3 weeks due pain
Pain 6/10 after 30 minutes of computer use
Poor wrist position with existing mouse setup
Goal: return to work without recurrence
Ergonomic education and neutral wrist positioning
Trialled vertical mouse and compact keyboard
Forearm stretching and graded endurance programme
Symptoms reduced with modified workstation trial
Pain 1-2/10 during one hour of simulated computer work
Tolerates two hours total desk work with scheduled breaks
Confident using vertical mouse and keyboard shortcuts
Week 1: 4 hours/day; Week 2: 6 hours/day; Week 3: usual hours if symptoms stable
Provide vertical mouse and compact keyboard
Permit regular microbreaks and task rotation
Review by occupational health if pain rises above 4/10
candidateLetter:
Mr David Price
Studio North Ltd
Nottingham

Hi David,

Re: Sophie

I am writing regarding my patient Ms Sophie Martin. She is married and lives at 7 Elm Terrace, Nottingham. She works as a graphic designer, 37.5 hours a week.

She has had right wrist and forearm pain for 4 months. Ultrasound no tendon tear. Unfortunately she was also diagnosed with carpal tunnel syndrome. She have been off work for 3 weeks because of the pain. I really feel sorry for her.

On 07/08/26 I seen her and her pain was 6/10 after 30 minutes of computer use. Her wrist position was poor with her mouse and she dont take many breaks. Then from 10 to 24 August we did lots of ergonomic stuff and stretches. She tried a vertical mouse and compact keybord and it helped a lot. She is now super confident with the vertical mouse and the keyboard shortcuts and has no night pain.

So she can go back to work gradually. Week 1 4 hours a day and in week 3 she will definitely be back to her normal hours. She should get a vertical mouse. Also she needs microbreaks. If pain is more then 7/10 she should see occupational health.

Let me know if you have any questions.

Cheers,
Occupational Therapist
